title.en: State the Doppler effect for sound
Explain why a moving source changes the wavelength

say.en: Stand beside a road as a motorbike roars past: its note is high as it comes and drops the moment it passes. The engine has not changed; what you hear has. In this lesson: State the Doppler effect for sound.
Explain why a moving source changes the wavelength.
Use f′ = f v over (v ∓ v s).

title.en: Crowded waves in front, stretched waves behind

body.en: A source of frequency f sends out one crest every 1/f second. If it moves at $v_s$ towards the listener, each new crest starts $v_s/f$ closer than the last, so the wavelength ahead is $\lambda' = (v - v_s)/f$. The speed of sound $v$ is fixed by the air, so the listener hears $f' = v/\lambda' = f\,\dfrac{v}{v - v_s}$. *Moving* away, the sign changes: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v}{v + v_s}$.

points.en: The speed of sound does not change
Ahead of the *source*: shorter λ, higher pitch

narration.en: A source of frequency f sends out one crest every 1/f second. If it moves at $v_s$ towards the listener, each new crest starts $v_s/f$ closer than the last, so the wavelength ahead is $\lambda' = (v - v_s)/f$. The speed of sound $v$ is fixed by the air, so the listener hears $f' = v/\lambda' = f\,\dfrac{v}{v - v_s}$. Moving away, the sign changes: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v}{v + v_s}$.

say.en: A source of frequency f sends out one crest every 1 over f second. If it moves at v s towards the listener, each new crest starts v s over f closer than the last, so the wavelength ahead is lambda ' equals v minus v s over f. The speed of sound v is fixed by the air, so the listener hears f' equals v over lambda ' equals f v over v minus v s. Moving away, the sign changes: f' equals f v over v plus v s. The speed of sound does not change.
Ahead of the source: shorter lambda, higher pitch.
Behind it: longer lambda, lower pitch.

narration.en: Each circle is a crest. When the source moves, the circles are no longer centred on the same point. Crests ahead come closer together, so the listener ahead hears a higher note.

caption.en: Each circle is a crest sent out once a second. Raise the source speed (as a fraction of the speed of sound) and see the crests crowd together in front and spread out behind.

title.en: Deriving f′ for a moving source

say.en: In one period T the first crest travels v T. The source travels v s T towards the listener.
The next crest starts from the new position, so the gap between crests is v T minus v s T.
The sound still travels at v, so f prime equals v over lambda prime.

problem.en: An ambulance siren of 800 Hz moves at 20 m/s. Find the frequency heard by a person standing ahead of it and by one behind it (v = 340 m/s).

narration.en: Let us solve this together. An ambulance siren of 800 Hz moves at 20 m/s. Find the frequency heard by a person standing ahead of it and by one behind it (v = 340 m/s).

say.en: Let us solve this together. An ambulance siren of 800 hertz moves at 20 metres per second. Find the frequency heard by a person standing ahead of it and by one behind it (v equals 340 metres per second).
Ahead: f' = 800 times 340 over 340 minus 20 equals 800 times 340 over 320 equals 850 hertz.
Behind: f' = 800 times 340 over 340 plus 20 equals 800 times 340 over 360 is approximately 755.6 hertz.
So the answer is 850 hertz ahead; about 756 hertz behind.

problem.en: A source moving towards a listener is heard at 1.2 times its real frequency. Find its speed (v = 330 m/s).

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A source moving towards a listener is heard at 1.2 times its real frequency. Find its speed (v = 330 m/s).

say.en: Let us solve this together. A source moving towards a listener is heard at 1.2 times its real frequency. Find its speed (v equals 330 metres per second).
1.2 equals v over (v - v s), so v - v s equals v over 1.2 equals 275 metres per second.
v s equals 330 minus 275 equals 55 metres per second.
So the answer is 55 metres per second.

points.en: The Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency due to motion of the source or the listener.
A moving source changes the wavelength: f′ = f v/(v − v_s) approaching, f v/(v + v_s) receding.
The speed of sound depends only on the medium.

title.en: Doppler effect: a moving listener, the general formula and uses

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. The Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency due to motion of the source or the listener.
A moving source changes the wavelength: f′ = f v over (v - v s) approaching, f v over v plus v s receding.
The speed of sound depends only on the medium.
